content: Acute bronchitis, commonly referred to as a chest cold, is a condition where the airways in the lungs become inflamed and produce mucus, leading to coughing. This condition is typically caused by a viral infection, although bacterial infections can occasionally be responsible. Antibiotics are not effective in treating viral chest colds and should not be used unless a bacterial cause is confirmed. Symptoms of Acute Bronchitis The hallmark symptom of acute bronchitis is a persistent cough, which may or may not produce mucus. Other symptoms can include: Chest discomfort or soreness. Fatigue or a general feeling of tiredness. Mild headaches. Mild muscle aches or body pain. A sore throat. These symptoms generally resolve within three weeks. Preventing Acute Bronchitis To reduce the risk of developing acute bronchitis, it is important to maintain good health practices, such as: Washing your hands frequently and thoroughly. Staying up to date with recommended vaccinations, including the influenza vaccine. Avoiding smoking and exposure to secondhand smoke. Covering your mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing to prevent the spread of germs. When to Seek Medical Attention You should consult a healthcare provider if you experience any of the following: A fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher. Coughing up mucus that contains blood. Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath. Symptoms that persist for more than three weeks. Recurrent episodes of bronchitis. For infants under three months old, a fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher requires immediate medical attention. Treatment of Acute Bronchitis Acute bronchitis typically resolves on its own without the need for antibiotics. Using antibiotics unnecessarily can lead to harmful side effects, such as allergic reactions, antimicrobial resistance, or severe infections like Clostridioides difficile (C. diff), which can cause life-threatening damage to the colon. Ways to Alleviate Symptoms To feel better while recovering from acute bronchitis, consider the following measures: Get adequate rest. Stay hydrated by drinking plenty of fluids. Use a clean humidifier or a cool mist vaporizer to ease breathing. Relieve nasal congestion with saline nasal sprays or drops. For young children, use a rubber suction bulb to clear mucus from their noses. Inhale steam from a bowl of hot water or a shower to soothe airways. Use throat lozenges or cough drops, but avoid giving lozenges to children under four years old. For adults and children over one year old, honey can help relieve coughing. Over-the-counter medications may provide temporary relief of symptoms, but they will not cure the illness. Always follow the instructions on medication labels and consult a healthcare provider for guidance, especially when giving medications to children. Over-the-Counter Medications for Children When using over-the-counter medications for children, it is crucial to follow age-specific guidelines: Pain relievers: For children under six months old, only acetaminophen is recommended. For children six months or older, both acetaminophen and ibuprofen are acceptable. Never give aspirin to children, as it can cause Reye's syndrome, a rare but serious condition that affects the liver and brain. Cough and cold medicines: Do not give over-the-counter cough and cold medications to children under four years old unless specifically directed by a healthcare provider, as these medications can cause severe and potentially life-threatening side effects in young children. For children aged four years or older, consult a healthcare provider to determine if these medications are safe and appropriate. Always inform your child’s healthcare provider about all medications, both prescription and over-the-counter, that your child is taking. Additionally, ask for guidance on the correct dosage based on your child’s age and weight. Similar Conditions Other illnesses, such as whooping cough (pertussis) or pneumonia, can present with symptoms similar to those of acute bronchitis. If you are diagnosed with whooping cough or pneumonia, your healthcare provider will likely prescribe antibiotics to treat the infection.
